quarterly_data.signal: BASF Q2 2026 call: CEO Markus Kamieth said EBITDA before special items rose 54% to EUR 2.4 billion on continued volume growth and higher margins, with earnings up in all segments except Surface Technologies (Battery Materials hit by expired subsidies, lower Precious Metal Services earnings); prices rose significantly after the Middle East escalation and the Strait of Hormuz blockade, especially upstream; volumes grew considerably in Greater China with the Zhanjiang Verbund ramp-up, European volume growth was almost 6% in Q2 'if I remember correctly', and North American volumes were slightly lower on the Port Arthur cracker turnaround. CFO Dirk Elvermann: H1 cash fixed costs fell about 4% to EUR 7.9 billion; Q2 operating cash flow was EUR 524 million and free cash flow minus EUR 189 million as higher prices tied up working capital.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 EBITDA before special items EUR 2.4 billion (+54%); H1 cash fixed costs EUR 7.9 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Outlook and plans (Q2 2026 call): CFO Dirk Elvermann expects Q3 earnings to at least meet Q3 2025, with potential for more depending on the macro environment, and Agricultural Solutions' Q3 earnings to meet or exceed last year despite South American sales pulled into Q2 ahead of an ERP conversion; capex payments are likely below the EUR 3.4 billion forecast, capex over the next four years will be 20% lower than in the prior planning period and stay below depreciation until 2028. CEO Markus Kamieth: the cost-savings program is on track for about EUR 2.3 billion of annual savings by year-end (EUR 2 billion run rate at end-June) with one-time costs of at least EUR 1.9 billion; the core businesses target up to 20% lower net cash fixed costs by 2029 versus 2024; Agricultural Solutions is on track for IPO readiness by mid-2027, though its prices stay under pressure for the rest of the year; Surface Technologies will be challenged in H2 without last year's 45X credits.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 earnings at least Q3 2025; savings about EUR 2.3 billion; capex below EUR 3.4 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Portfolio (Q2 2026 call, CEO Markus Kamieth): the Coatings transaction with Carlyle closed on June 30 and BASF now holds a 40% equity share in Surventis; BASF reduced its stake in Harbour Energy to under 25% of the voting shares through the sale of 80 million shares in March 2026, a block sale of 150 million shares in May 2026 and smaller market sales, and intends to exit that financial investment over time; AgBiTech, a biological insect-control company, was acquired in March. He sees M&A becoming more competitive against large organic capacity expansions as chemical-industry consolidation accelerates.
quarterly_data.figure: 40% stake in Surventis; Harbour Energy stake under 25%

quarterly_data.signal: Management views (Q2 2026 call): CEO Markus Kamieth said BASF kept supply uninterrupted through its local-for-local footprint, flex-feed steam crackers and feedstock trading, a 'pressure test' it passed; certain Middle East capacities will be out of the market for a longer period, but chemical markets have adjusted and China upstream margins have normalized to pre-war levels; he has seen no demand destruction and July came in as expected; record-low Rhine water levels will cause some disruption in European value chains, but specialized low-water ships leave BASF much better prepared than in 2018. CFO Dirk Elvermann said hedging and the feedstock trading desk lifted Q2 results in Other. Kamieth criticised the EU ETS reform proposal's shift toward making relief conditional on investment commitments.
